name: Lateral meniscus — anterior horn
description: Anterior third of the nearly circular lateral meniscus, its root attaching just lateral to and partly beneath the ACL footprint. A low-signal triangle about the same height as the lateral posterior horn, often striated near the root where ACL fibers interleave.

normal_values.height_vs_posterior_horn: about equal to the lateral posterior horn on sagittal images

variants_pitfalls: Speckled signal near the root is normal (ACL fibers and fat between root fibers; 7 of 11 volunteers) and can span two images, so judge the horn's shape and whether the signal stays at the root beside the ACL.
A horn clearly taller than the posterior horn, with a small or truncated posterior horn, is a flipped posterior horn fragment (double anterior horn), usually lateral.
The inferior lateral genicular artery runs with fat along the outer edge and can mimic a peripheral tear; it lies outside the meniscal triangle and is tubular on adjacent images.
Where the transverse ligament joins the horn, the fat between them can mimic an oblique tear; follow the ligament medially.
After ACL reconstruction check the root: the ACL covers about 63% of its footprint, and a 10 mm tibial reamer breached it in 4 of 6 cadaver knees.
